name: Alur
region: West Nile, Uganda (Nebbi, Zombo, Pakwach) and across the border in Ituri, DR Congo
translator_note: Built from Alur's shared Luo vocabulary (Acholi, Lango, Dholuo cognates) in the everyday spoken register of a young Nebbi or Zombo professional: bare imperatives on buttons (Wot, Ribo, Kodi, Oro), the impersonal ju- subject for things done to the user (juculo = it has been paid), the Alur negative ngo, and the possessives para/peri/pere. App-era concepts use the loans West Nile speech already carries (motoka, siteji, simu, pesa, app, link, kodi, sandbox, plug-in). No native reviewer has read this: verb-final vowels (-o/-u) and the imperative forms in particular need checking, and every long paragraph is a close paraphrase rather than a sentence-by-sentence rendering.
